title: Phoenix · Apache Trail and Salt River
slogan: A 294 km loop out of Tortilla Flat
story: Desert light, canyon roads and heat discipline. This road trip is shaped as a ride, not as a shortcut: leave the start cleanly, use the first checkpoint for fuel and weather discipline, then let the middle 118 km be the part you remember. The best part sits around Apache Trail overlook, Roosevelt Lake, while Globe fuel and Tortilla Flat keep the day practical instead of turning it into a fuel hunt. Check the selected map before departure: scenic sections, transfer sections, speed/control reminders, risk points and the GPX checkpoint order are deliberately visible so the route is understandable before the engine starts. Ride it early if the area is popular, keep the photo stops legal, and shorten the route if weather, daylight or energy stops agreeing with the plan.

sections.advice: Use Phoenix start → Tortilla Flat (72 km) as clean positioning. Keep it tidy, ignore impatient traffic and save the enthusiasm for the good road ahead. The value here is not drama; it is arriving at the riding section with space, fuel and concentration intact.

sections.advice: This Roosevelt Lake → Globe fuel stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

scenicChapters.title: Apache Trail
scenicChapters.narrative: For 18 km this is Apache Trail, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Apache Trail
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 45 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.
